title: 21-23. THE BOY CANNOT LEAVE HIS FATHER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then you said to your servants, "Bring him down to me so I can see him for myself." And we said to my lord, "The boy cannot leave his father; if he leaves him, his father will die." But you told your servants, "Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again."'" — Gen 44:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah is carefully retelling the whole story, step by step. He is not arguing. He is not disputing the facts. He is simply laying out the situation so that this powerful man will understand what is really at stake: an old man's life.

"If he leaves him, his father will die." That is the heart of Judah's plea. He is not pleading for Benjamin's comfort or his own freedom. He is pleading for his father.

This is a man who has learned to think about someone other than himself. The Judah of Genesis 37 was worried about profit. The Judah of Genesis 44 is worried about his father's heart.

There is a good pattern here for our own prayers. So much of what we bring to God is about our own comfort — and He welcomes that, because He is a Father. But there is a maturity that grows in us over time, where our prayers begin to carry other people's burdens more than our own. Where we start pleading for a father, a friend, a wayward child, a struggling church.

Jesus prayed that way in John 17, spending His final hours praying for others. He prays for us still (Heb 7:25).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How much of your prayer life is about others compared to yourself?
2. Whose burden could you carry to God this week?
3. What does it mean to you that Jesus is praying for you right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to carry other people's burdens the way Judah carried his father's. Thank You that Jesus lives to intercede for me even when I forget to pray. Amen.
